children: The White House said in a letter to Politico on Tuesday that last week’s revocation of the outlet’s press pass was an "unusual step" because the news organization had violated professional standards, including the use of anonymous sources, spreading verifiable false information about national security, and publishing sensitive or classified information. According to Sina Finance, citing The Washington Post, one of the alleged violations cited in the letter was an article that was actually written based on a White House-hosted media call, and a recording of the call showed reporters were told to cite an anonymous "senior government official" when relaying the information to the public.

The letter, which referenced the report, was one of three documents the government filed in court on Tuesday to defend its decision to bar Politico, CNN, and MS NOW from the White House campus. According to the White House letter, one of Politico’s six alleged violations was a June 2026 article that opened with a quote from a "senior government official" and detailed efforts aimed at ending the war in Iran.

title: White House Bars Politico Reporter Over Anonymous Sources and Sensitive Information
